# s2opc / decode_fuzzer

s2opc's own fuzz target `decode_fuzzer` ([source](source/fuzz_decoder.c), unmodified), one of the targets OSS-Fuzz builds, over S2OPC (gitlab.com/systerel/S2OPC at bad930a6).

Checks 2 properties (listed below); the first, an API contract: For a fuzz-selected OPC UA encodeable type (6 type groups, byte 0/1 select group/type), if Decode of the input succeeds then Encode of the decoded value must succeed, and Decode of that encoding must succeed.

## How this program differs from what OSS-Fuzz runs
- Linked against S2OPC at commit bad930a6.
- In every build, getenv() returns NULL, getpid() returns 1 and mkstemp() uses a fixed name, so the program depends only on its input.
- A small driver reads the input file, calls the harness one to four times and prints each return value.

## What the harness checks
- For a fuzz-selected OPC UA encodeable type (6 type groups, byte 0/1 select group/type), if Decode of the input succeeds then Encode of the decoded value must succeed, and Decode of that encoding must succeed ([lines 125-158](source/fuzz_decoder.c#L125-L158)): assert(); confirmed in the binary.
- decode(x)=v, encode(v)=b1, decode(b1)=v2, encode(v2)=b2: b1 and b2 must be byte-identical (length and memcmp), i.e. encode.decode is idempotent on the canonical encoding (the input itself is deliberately not compared) ([line 161](source/fuzz_decoder.c#L161)): assert(); confirmed in the binary.

A failed check marked as ending the process contradicts every halts statement below, so a proof of one implies them on every input it covers.

## Builds
Static riscv64 Linux programs, compiled for RV64G and run as `<file> <input-file>`; `oft fetch s2opc` downloads the published ones and checks each against its SHA-256.

| build | file | bytes | sha256 |
|---|---|---:|---|
| plain | `decode_fuzzer.plain` | 226,248 | `77ba3c36c5ffac2db12ddb3919939672ba0063d0f10ddf7aba26cf6b25692621` |
| ubsan | `decode_fuzzer.ubsan` | 241,192 | `a762fb5c5e0615ac1ff2e3d4782571d81930a20e0d21c3b9b9e71355da033ce1` |
| asan | `decode_fuzzer.asan` | 985,176 | `e04adedd3473ea918d6a642391bf93cf6e7627f823901c3b20db9f35c2794c5b` |
| asan-ubsan | `decode_fuzzer.asan-ubsan` | 986,232 | `828f14f065ee5a7d469bb9bb66dac0100838e4c73925c25b37f7b7c91488724f` |

Each build also links code that no sanitizer instruments, as its link recorded it. A statement about a sanitizer build covers that code only as uninstrumented code: ASan checks no load or store made inside it, and UBSan inserts no check there.

- plain: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library)
- ubsan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library)
- asan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.asan.a` (the sanitizer runtime), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library), `libunwind.a` (the C++ runtime)
- asan-ubsan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.asan.a` (the sanitizer runtime), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library), `libunwind.a` (the C++ runtime)
